title: Typed Capability Completion and Replacement Cutover Evidence Contracts

preflight.note: Recorded before RepoPact implementation work began. Origin: ForgeWire ADR 0010 / INV-4 and the 2026-08-22 production-reachability audit; this item is research/reconciliation-first and does not authorize a predetermined schema design.

acceptance_criteria.text: A durable field-evidence capture classifies the repeated completion/cutover failure shapes from ForgeWire ADR 0010 / INV-4, WI233, and WI239-WI246, separating product-unreachable implementations, incomplete replacements, synthetic-success/degraded paths, experimental-vs-product claims, duplicate authorities, no-op advertised actions, and known-breach architectural migrations. The capture records which observations are ForgeWire-specific and which are plausible generic governance classes.

The work formally reconciles the candidate completion/claim-closure concept with RepoPact's existing H14 enforcement-closure model (coverage, invocation, effectiveness). It states whether the concepts are distinct, overlapping, or reducible; it does not rewrite H14 retroactively. If a new hypothesis/property is warranted, it is preregistered with prospective falsification criteria before any benchmark result is counted as support.

Before any kernel/schema implementation, at least four candidate record placements are evaluated: work-item-level claim, acceptance-criterion-level claim, evidence-run-level typing, and a separate claim/evidence-contract record (or an explicitly justified equivalent set). The chosen design records why its placement, extensibility, reference semantics, and lifecycle are preferable and explicitly rejects simply hard-coding ForgeWire's INV-4 vocabulary into every adopter.

The chosen generic model can express a capability-completion claim whose required evidence includes a real production/application entry or composition path and composition/end-to-end proof of that path, plus explicit degraded/unavailable behavior when relevant; an implementation/service plus green unit tests alone is representable as insufficient rather than product-complete.

The chosen generic model can express a replacement/cutover claim whose evidence establishes replacement implementation, caller migration, predecessor retirement/unreachability, and a static or contract-level absence guard preventing predecessor reintroduction. A replacement that leaves the predecessor load-bearing or available as an accidental fallback is rejected by a negative fixture when this claim type is used.

The work decides how fail-closed/degraded-success truthfulness relates to completion evidence: an operation that did not actually persist, deliver, or execute cannot silently satisfy a success-shaped completion proof. The decision either incorporates typed/unambiguous degraded outcomes into the generic claim contract or records a separate upstream work item with rationale.

The resulting RepoPact contract is additive/opt-in for existing repositories and historical completed work unless a separate explicit breaking-version decision is accepted. Existing work items without typed completion claims remain valid under current semantics; experimental/library-only work can remain intentionally production-unreachable when it is explicitly classified rather than represented as product-complete.

After AC-1 through AC-3 choose the abstraction, the selected model is implemented consistently across the necessary schema/validator/SPEC/template/documentation/conformance surfaces. Derived artifacts are regenerated rather than hand-maintained, and any frozen-surface change follows the existing approval contract.

Conformance/regression coverage contains positive and negative cases for at least: a production-reachable capability with composition proof; a service with only unit tests and no production path; a complete replacement; a replacement whose predecessor remains reachable; a replacement missing an absence guard; and explicitly experimental/unavailable capability state that is not falsely promoted to product-complete.

The chosen abstraction is validated against ForgeWire-shaped cases and at least one non-ForgeWire synthetic/adopter-neutral fixture. Closeout evidence explains what would falsify the claim that the abstraction is generic rather than overfit to ForgeWire's architecture.

A durable upstream-candidate disposition matrix covers at minimum: known-breach shrink-only ratchets; canonical-record/human-representation parity (including F-016); concurrent work-item identifier allocation; and fail-closed success semantics. Each is either incorporated here with explicit justification, linked to an existing RepoPact finding/work item, spawned as a separate proposed work item, or rejected as adopter-specific with rationale. WI042/F-015 and WI043/F-017 remain separate and are not taken over by WI044.
